Here is a draft for the WhatsApp message. It incorporates his artistic and activist background while seamlessly weaving in your technical experience with agentic workflows and the local environment.
Hey Oz! 👋 I've been following your work, and I was thinking about how you could absolutely supercharge your murals and activism using some of the new agentic AI workflows. I put together 10 ideas on how you could use tools like OpenClaw, OpenCode, and Gemini to scale your art and community impact:
1. Community Story Gathering (OpenClaw)
You can deploy OpenClaw to a dedicated WhatsApp number. When you're planning a community mural, locals in Asunción can text the bot their stories or neighborhood issues. OpenClaw acts as your local agent, gathering and summarizing these voices to inspire the theme of your next piece.
2. Deep Lore Research (Gemini)
You can drop massive, obscure PDFs on Guarani mythology or local political history directly into Gemini. With its huge context window, it can instantly cross-reference texts and suggest highly accurate symbols to weave into your 90s-comic-style compositions.
3. Coding Interactive Mural Apps (OpenCode)
You don't need to be a developer to add tech to your walls. You can use OpenCode in your terminal to autonomously build a lightweight AR app or an interactive website. Visitors scan a QR code on your mural, and the OpenCode-built site animates your characters or plays a soundtrack.
4. Automating NGO Proposals (OpenClaw + Gemini)
Since you work with orgs like the UN Human Rights Office, you can have Gemini draft the formal proposals, and then ask your OpenClaw assistant to automatically format the documents and email them to the right directors while you're out painting.
5. Supply Logistics via WhatsApp (OpenClaw)
Managing big walls means juggling scaffolding, spray paint inventory, and budgets. Because OpenClaw integrates with your own chat apps, you can just text it: "Update my spreadsheet: bought 20 Montana cans for 1.5M PYG," and it handles the database and currency conversions in the background.
6. Rapid Concept Iteration
Before touching a wall, you can use image generation models to test your bold, anti-corruption concepts and Guarani hybrids directly over photos of real streets and building facades to see how the colors pop in the physical environment.
7. Custom Inventory Trackers (OpenCode)
If you need a specific tool to track international commissions or upcoming street art festivals, OpenCode can read your requirements and write the entire codebase for a custom management dashboard while you focus on the art.
8. Agentic News Scraping
You can set up a daily automated workflow where an AI agent scrapes local news for specific topics—like indigenous land rights or corruption cases. It can deliver a weekly digest of visual metaphors to ensure your street art remains sharply responsive to current events.
9. Collaborative Style Transfer
During your community workshops, you can use local image-to-image models to let kids upload their own simple sketches and instantly see them rendered in your signature heavy-ink, pop-surrealist style.
10. Auto-Archiving Your Work (OpenClaw)
Once a mural is done, you can text the photo to your OpenClaw bot. It can automatically resize the image, generate tags based on the location and theme, and push it straight to your digital portfolio or Instagram.
Let me know if you want to grab a coffee or a bite around Central and set any of these up! I’ve been building a lot of agentic orchestrators and SaaS tools lately, and I'd love to help you rig up a local workspace. 🇵🇾🎨
